title: Phased cut criteria and release communications lattice for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Define a phased cut criteria framework and a release communications lattice to coordinate launch activities across the Redwood API, Console, and Runtime teams. Deliverables include a decision ladder for scope cuts, clearly defined safety fences, a comms matrix for internal and external stakeholders, and a release-note sync cadence to minimize last-minute churn.
milestones: M1: Scope finalization and lane mapping - 2025-02-24
M2: Canary configuration and perf SLO sign-off - 2025-03-03
M3: Docs & release notes draft freeze - 2025-03-07
scope_lanes: Lane A (Must ship): API surface parity, auth/backwards compatibility, basic telemetry
Lane B (High value): Console UX for rollout, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns
Lane C (Optional): Runtime knob for aggressive batching, experimental quantization profiles
cut_criteria: Severity-first: Any change that increases error-rate by >0.5% in perf lab or causes client-visible 5xx regressions is a hard cut
SLO-first: Feature removal required if added latency pushes 95p token latency above SLA for Dedicated customers
Test coverage gate: New code must have unit + e2e tests and an integration test in the canary harness
Documentation gate: Public API or Console changes require updated user docs and sample snippets before inclusion
cut_triggers_and_actions: Trigger: Canary flakiness spike (>3 incidents / 24h) -> Action: Pause rollout, trigger rollback plan, notify incident channel
Trigger: Blocker bug found in runtime quantization path -> Action: Revert quantized artifacts, shift traffic to verified variant
Trigger: Doc/UX misalignment discovered -> Action: Roll back Console changes, fast-track doc edits and ship in next micro-release
communications_matrix: Audience: All-redwood Slack #release-commits -> Message cadence: daily updates during M2-M5, final pre-launch note 24h before
Audience: Sales & Customer Success -> Message cadence: embargoed release notes and feature impact matrix 72h before launch
Audience: Public changelog -> Message cadence: release notes published at T+0 with migration guide and known issues
release_notes_coordination: Week -3: PM authors feature summary + impact statement
Week -2: Eng provides risk bullets, perf numbers, and rollout knobs
Week -1: Design supplies screenshots and interactions; Docs drafts published to drive
Freeze: Docs and release notes enter review queue 4 business days before launch
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal-only rollout to staging and canary groups with synthetic load
Phase 1: 5% production traffic on non-critical routes for 48h
Phase 2: 25% traffic with feature flags; collect telemetry and health signals
Phase 3: 100% gradual ramp with post-launch monitor at +1h, +6h, +24h
safety_fences: Automatic fallback: Route-level fallback to compatible model variant when latency > threshold
Kill switches: Per-cluster kill switch controlled by SRE with documented rollback steps
Monitoring: Runbook with top-5 signals (5xx rate, 95p latency, error types, resource saturation, KV cache miss rate)

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Last-minute perf regression in Dedicated - Mitigation: Holdback knob + targeted rollbacks and extended canary
Risk: Ambiguous API changes break downstream customers - Mitigation: Strict compatibility checks and expanded integration test matrix
Risk: Docs lag behind UI changes - Mitigation: Block merge until docs PR is linked and reviewed
acceptance_criteria: All lane A items merged or explicitly scoped out with owner & timeline
Performance regression < 0.2% on core bench for canary traffic profile
Release notes drafted, reviewed by Eng/Design/Docs, and approved by PM
Rollback and kill-switch playbooks validated in dry-run with SRE
